question: True or false: cyclists given only dummy capsules produced more power the higher the caffeine dose they were told they had taken?
answer: True. Beedie and colleagues gave trained cyclists placebo capsules before 10 km time trials. Told they had taken none, they produced 1.4% less power than baseline; told 4.5 mg per kg, 1.3% more; told 9 mg per kg, 3.1% more. Belief alone traced a dose-response curve, from an empty capsule.
move: Without a dummy version to compare against, a result also measures hope.
trap: Assuming a capsule with nothing in it can do nothing.
source: Beedie et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2006
reference: Beedie, Stuart, Coleman & Foad, Placebo effects of caffeine on cycling performance, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 2006
